# Cauchy–Schwarz — Bound a Dot Product

## The identity to remember

$$
(a_1b_1+\cdots+a_nb_n)^2\le(a_1^2+\cdots+a_n^2)(b_1^2+\cdots+b_n^2)
$$

**Every symbol explained:** n is number of components; a_i,b_i are real entries of two vectors; dots continue the same pattern; the left is squared dot product, the right multiplies squared lengths.

**Substitute actual numbers:** Let a=(3,4), b=(1,0). Dot product is 3. Left squared is 9. Right is (9+16)(1+0)=25, so 9≤25.

## Why it is true

For real vectors, consider the always-nonnegative quadratic ||a−tb||² in scalar t. Its discriminant cannot be positive if b≠0, yielding (a·b)²≤||a||²||b||².

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

Use to bound correlations, projections and extremal sums. For unit vectors, their dot product lies between −1 and 1.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

Equality occurs when the vectors are linearly dependent. Be careful with empty vectors and zero length when dividing by a norm.

## Your turn

Find the strongest bound on 2x+3y if x²+y²=1.

**Memory rule:** Translate the inequality into a statement about maximum, minimum or impossible values, then prove it.
